rules.title: Dependants
rules.text: Most students on taught courses, including taught master’s degrees, can no longer bring family members. Dependants are generally only allowed for postgraduate research courses such as PhDs.

rules.title: Working while you study
rules.text: Degree-level students can usually work up to 20 hours a week in term time and full time in vacations.

rules.title: After your course
rules.text: You may be able to switch to the [Graduate visa](/graduate-visa/) to stay and work.

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: Student visa UK requirements
sections.text: You need an unconditional offer and a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from a licensed student sponsor, enough money for your course fees and living costs held for at least 28 days, English at the required level, a valid passport, a tuberculosis test certificate if you are from a listed country, and parental consent if you are under 18.

faqs.q: How much money do I need for a Student visa UK?
faqs.a: Your course fees for the first year plus living costs for up to 9 months, at the rate for where you’ll study. The funds must be held for 28 days.

faqs.q: Can I bring my family on a Student visa?
faqs.a: Usually only if you are on a postgraduate research course, such as a PhD.
Degree-level students can usually work up to 20 hours a week in term time.
